concept_weaknesses: The proposed 70% DIBELS benchmark-level gain target needs a rationale, baseline information, and a clear explanation of how it will be measured.
The concept does not describe how it will recruit, train, schedule, and retain 40 tutors to serve 120 students twice weekly, or how the proposed work fits available staff capacity.
The organization lists MOUs with two schools, but the concept proposes expansion to a third school; confirm the partnership and access to students.
The family-night attendance target would be stronger with a participation plan and a clear definition of how attendance will be tracked.
unsupported_claims: “Our tutoring model produced gains for most students in 2025” is not substantiated by the listed evidence, which notes pre/post DIBELS assessments for 241 students but provides no results.
“Our program is proven to double reading growth” is not supported by the listed evidence, which contains no comparison or growth-rate findings.
The claim that fewer than half of K-3 students at partner schools read at grade level relies on school-reported data that is not included in the listed evidence assets.
concerns: The application requires two letters of support; availability is not stated.
The supplied source gives a December 15, 2026 deadline, while the opportunity metadata has no deadline; confirm the deadline and submission details with the funder.
The requested $60,000 is within the stated $25,000–$75,000 range, and the budget line items total $60,000.
rationale: The organization meets the stated hard criteria: it is a 501(c)(3), its $850,000 annual budget is below the $3 million limit, and it serves Connecticut residents. The literacy and family-engagement focus aligns with the stated priorities, and the requested amount and 12-month timeline fit the funding terms. Strengthen the evidence, third-school partnership, implementation plan, and required support materials before submitting.
